reason: The immediate goal is to shelter the water line, and wrapping it in reflective quilt stock seems a direct way to reduce heat loss.
expectation: I expect an insulated water line, though it may need further protection.

alternatives.reason: Wall blocks seem relevant to the protective shell, but the quilt appears more directly useful for the water line first.

effect: The quilt made an insulated water line, so it may now need a protective covering or placement.
reason: The shovel and insulated line are compatible, suggesting I can bury the line to shelter it.
expectation: I expect to bury or cover the insulated water line, though I am unsure exactly how.

alternatives.reason: Making wall blocks also fits the chapter's shell-building goal, but sheltering the water line is the current goal.

effect: The line is sheltered with accessible connections, though its heat tracing still needs power. The new goal calls for a protective structure that does not load the cabin skin.
reaction: The distinction between insulation slowing heat loss and heat tracing needing power was useful.
reason: Making wall blocks seems relevant to the new goal, and it is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the furnace mold to turn the graded regolith into blocks for a freestanding protective wall, though further assembly will likely be needed.

effect: The graded regolith became interlocking wall blocks, ready to use around the cabin.
reason: Placing the blocks at the cabin perimeter is the only available combination and seems like the next step toward protecting the cabin.
expectation: I expect a protective wall around the cabin, possibly with a gap so it does not load the cabin skin.

effect: The wall stands on its own footing, leaving the pressure shell clear and providing support for packed local material.
reaction: The separate footing makes the goal of avoiding a load on the cabin clear.
reason: The shovel and wall are the only available combination, and the result suggests packing local material against the wall.
expectation: I expect to pile or pack local material against the freestanding wall to improve the cabin's shelter.

effect: The packed material completed the cabin shelter, and the heater cycling off suggests reduced heating demand while the window remains usable.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the shelter have a visible effect on the cabin.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the freestanding wall was most worthwhile because its separate footing made the reason for keeping the load off the pressure shell clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the interlocking blocks was straightforward but had little detail on its own.

surprise.text: I learned that the water line's insulation slows heat loss, while its heat tracing still needs power.

arbitrary.text: The shovel-and-line combination was initially a guess because the option did not say it would create a trench; the result made its purpose clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I am curious how the expedition develops, and the distinction between insulation and powered heat tracing gave me something useful to think about.
